assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing to stable GLP-1 receptor agonists, has produced a new class of therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery chain is clear, original and of very large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and active GLP-1(7-36) form, Mojsov identified the active peptide and its insulinotropic role, and Drucker defined the biology and the therapeutic pharmacology, including GLP-2. Knudsen's drug-development role is major but industrial; the credit among Mojsov, Habener and others is contested, and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many large randomized outcome trials, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over the identification of active GLP-1 and the allocation of credit between academic discoverers and drug developers.
Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still being established; I have not independently verified trial details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed by innate immunity, linking infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies, cancer immunity and senescence. It is a conceptual advance with wide disease relevance, and it connects directly to the type I interferon biology seen in autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide 2'3'-cGAMP second messenger, which is the decisive step. Barber discovered STING. Sun, Wu and Ishikawa made contributions in the Chen and Barber laboratories but are the more junior contributors, so a two-person configuration seems fairest.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is reproduced across many laboratories and structural studies and is well accepted. Therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still immature, but the discovery itself is mature enough.
uncertainties: Whether STING and cGAS should be recognized together with earlier DNA-sensing work by others.
Clinical translation has so far been modest; I have not independently verified current trial status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is the dominant upstream cytokine in rheumatoid arthritis, and that blocking it gives clinical benefit, turned a disabling disease into a treatable one and established cytokine-targeted therapy across inflammatory disease. The path from mechanism to patients is exceptionally clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translational concept and the first clinical trials, using the cytokine cascade work on synovial cultures. Contributions from others on TNF biology and antibody engineering exist, but the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across several indications and drugs. Fully mature, and recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Attribution relative to those who discovered or cloned TNF itself and those who built the antibodies; the supplied credit may under-represent them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that redirect immunity against cancer produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept of engineering receptors is original and the clinical effect is striking.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain developed the CD28 costimulatory CAR design and the preclinical concept, June led the 4-1BB CAR trials that led to the first approvals, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified lymphocytes. Other early contributors, such as Eshhar, are not in the supplied credit, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year follow-up show durable benefit in hematological cancers. Solid tumour efficacy and safety are still limited, so the field is maturing rather than complete.
uncertainties: Omission of early chimeric-receptor pioneers from the supplied credit.
Limited success in solid tumours and toxicity; I have not independently verified long-term outcome data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified the peptide system that stabilizes wakefulness and showed that its loss causes narcolepsy type 1, linking a defined neuropeptide to a human sleep disorder. It has led to orexin receptor antagonists for insomnia and agonists in development.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai discovered orexin and its receptors and the narcolepsy phenotype in knockouts; de Lecea and Kilduff discovered hypocretin independently with a different focus; Mignot identified the canine hypocretin receptor 2 mutation and the human deficiency. Three laureates cannot cover all of these, so this is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, with approved drugs, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery of hypocretin by de Lecea and colleagues versus orexin by Yanagisawa and Sakurai creates a credit dilemma.
The autoimmune basis of narcolepsy type 1 is still unproven; I am relying on my own recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not just proliferation, drives cancer, defined the apoptosis-regulating family, and underpinned venetoclax for leukaemia. A foundational concept with real clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the cloning and characterization of the BCL-2 family, and Vaux showed that BCL-2 inhibits cell death and cooperates with MYC. Strasser contributed to later mechanisms. The Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer contributions are also important and not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Established for decades and supported by an approved targeted drug. Mature, although apoptosis was partly recognized in the 2002 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier apoptosis recognition and the omission of Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer (deceased) from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term adult stem cell-derived organoids from single Lgr5+ cells provided a general platform for modelling tissue biology, infection, cancer and patient-specific drug response. The impact on experimental medicine is wide.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem cell identification and the organoid culture; Sato was first author and developed the intestinal organoid method. This is a compact and plausible two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted across laboratories, but clinical translation (personalized medicine, regenerative use) is still maturing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether organoids are judged to be a tool rather than a discovery, relative to other candidates.
Overlap with pluripotent stem cell-derived organoid work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions of precancerous lesions that are already documented. It is a clear example of prevention of cancer by vaccination.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP technology at the NCI, and Frazer, with Zhou, did the early VLP expression work; Zhou (deceased) is not in the supplied credit. The three names appear to fit a fair prize, though priority between groups has been contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong evidence from long-term vaccine effectiveness and registry data. Timely, with the cancer outcome data now accumulating.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between the NCI, Queensland and other groups, and the omission of Jian Zhou.
The effect on invasive cancer endpoints is still accumulating; I have not independently verified population data.
